direct_answer: Caring for someone with arthritis and frailty can be physically and emotionally tiring. Signs of burnout include exhaustion, poor sleep, low mood and irritability. A carer's assessment, respite, sharing tasks and looking after your own health can help.

content:
Many carers help with washing, dressing, moving, appointments and medicines. Over time, this can affect the carer's own body, sleep and mood.

This guide is for carers and explains signs of burnout and where to get help. It is educational information, not medical advice.

Signs of burnout

  • Feeling exhausted most of the time.
  • Poor sleep, headaches or back pain.
  • Feeling irritable, tearful, hopeless or resentful.
  • Withdrawing from friends.
  • Neglecting your own health appointments.

Practical help

  • Ask your council for a carer's assessment. You have a right to one if you appear to need support.
  • Ask about respite or replacement care so you can take breaks.
  • Get equipment and training for moving and handling to protect your back.
  • Tell your GP you are a carer.
  • Share tasks with family or friends where possible.

Looking after yourself

Short daily breaks, regular meals, staying active and keeping in touch with others help. If your mood is low, talk to your GP or self-refer to NHS talking therapies in England.

When to get help

  • Call 999 if anyone is in immediate danger.
  • Get urgent help if you are having thoughts of suicide: call NHS 111, your GP, or Samaritans on 116 123.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

What is a carer's assessment?

An assessment by the council of the support you need as a carer.

Can I get money as a carer?

You may be eligible for Carer's Allowance. Check GOV.UK or get benefits advice.

Where can I talk to someone?

Carers UK has a helpline and online support.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Help and support for carers
  • Carers UK
  • NHS: NHS Talking Therapies for anxiety and depression
  • GOV.UK: Apply for a needs assessment by social services
